The HTML file is not a document that opens an app: it is the app. The code, fonts and charts are all inside it, and nothing is downloaded when you use it.

Setting up: about ten minutes

  1. Extract the ZIP into a folder you will find again. A synced folder (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) is ideal.
  2. Double-click NetWorthFireTracker.html. It opens in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox like a web page, and works offline from then on.
  3. Take the welcome tour. A few short slides on adding accounts, the monthly check-in, your FIRE number and backups.
  4. Add your accounts with today’s balance: checking, savings, investments, retirement, your home, and what you owe. The usual ones are one click away on an empty app.
  5. Set your FIRE number on the FIRE plan: enter what you spend in a year.
  6. Download a backup from Settings & backup. Page 9 explains why it matters more than anything else here.

Want to look around first?

Choose Explore sample data on the welcome screen or in Settings & backup. A fictional household’s 13 accounts and two and a half years of check-ins fill every screen, in a separate session. Return to my accounts brings back your own, untouched.

The idea

One number that counts.

Net worth is everything you own minus everything you owe. Watch it once a month and it tells you if you’re moving in the right direction.

Net worth. The big number, what moved since last month, and how far along you are to your FIRE number; the ring shows where what you own sits.

WordWhat it means
Net worthWhat you own minus what you owe.
Toward FIInvested money that can pay for your life one day: investments, retirement accounts, an HSA, crypto.
FIRE numberA year of spending ÷ your withdrawal rate. At 4% that’s 25 years of spending.
Coast FIEnough invested that, with no more saving, it grows into your FIRE number by retirement age.

Adding accounts

Add each account once.

Accounts → Add an account. Typing a name picks the type for you; a name like “Visa” or “Mortgage” switches to something you owe.

FieldWhat to enter
Name“Checking”, “401(k)”, “Mortgage”. Anything you’ll recognize.
Own or oweSomething you own (an asset) or something you owe (a debt).
Balance todayWhat it’s worth, or what you owe, as a positive number. $35,000 or 1,250.50 are fine.
TypeCash, savings, investments, retirement, HSA, crypto, home, vehicle, mortgage, cards, loans. Add your own in Settings.
Counts toward FITicked for investments and retirement accounts. Change it per account.
Bank, noteOptional: where it’s held, a reminder like “employer matches 4%”.

Your home and car

Add them at a fair estimate if you like: they count in your net worth, but not toward FI, because you can’t live off them without selling.

Closing or paying off

Edit the account and set it to Closed or paid off with the month. It counts as 0 from then, and keeps its history.

Each month

A two-minute check-in.

Once a month, open Monthly check-in, type each balance as it is today, and save.

Watch it as you type

The totals at the top and each row’s change update as you type, so you see the month before you save.

Missed a month?

No problem: a month without a check-in keeps the last balances. Use the arrows to fill in an earlier month whenever you like.

Only one account changed? Use Update balance on its card instead.

Your FIRE number

How much is enough?

FIRE plan → enter a year of spending. Everything else has a sensible default you can change.

Withdrawal rateHow much of your invested money you’d spend each year. 4% is the classic rule; 3.5% is more cautious.
Return after inflationA steady average growth rate in today’s money. 5% is a middle-of-the-road guess.
Invested each monthEverything going into accounts that count toward FI, employer match included.
Lean, FIRE, Fat75%, 100% and 150% of your spending, each with its own date.

The road there

When could you stop working?

The road there draws your invested money growing year by year against your FIRE number.

What moves the date

Spend 10% less, invest more, lower returns, a safer withdrawal rate: each one shows how much sooner or later.

What if?

Slide What if you invested more each month? and a second line shows the difference.

It’s a smooth average, not a promise: real markets go up and down. Your check-ins keep it honest.

Read this one

Keeping your numbers safe.

Everything lives in your browser, on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account, and nobody else holds a copy, including us.

Your entries live in browser storage: please read

  • Everything you enter or import is saved automatically in that browser's local storage.
  • Clearing your cache, history or site data will permanently delete it.
  • It does not carry across browsers: data added in Chrome will not appear in Safari.
  • The HTML file does not contain your entries. Copying the file does not copy your data.

Do one of these. Ideally both.

Download backup: every browser

Settings & backup → Download backup. One JSON file holding every account, check-in, account type and your FIRE plan. Restore backup brings it back on any computer. The app reminds you when a backup is due.

Daily folder backup: Chrome or Edge

Choose a synced folder once (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) and a dated copy is written each day you make changes. Safari and Firefox do not offer this; use Download backup instead.

Moving to another computer

Copy the HTML file and your latest backup across, open the file, then Settings & backup → Restore backup.

When you need help

A few useful fixes.

What you seeWhat to do
It opens as code, not an appExtract the ZIP first, then right-click the file → Open with → your browser.
My numbers are goneCheck it is the same browser and profile you used before. Otherwise, Restore backup.
My net worth jumpedCheck the newest check-in for a typo: History → open the month, or the account’s own history.
Toward FI is $0Edit your investment and retirement accounts and tick Counts toward financial independence.
Years to FI says “not at this rate”Nothing is going in and nothing grows: add what you invest each month, or a return above 0%.
A debt shows as negativeEnter what you owe as a positive number on a “Something I owe” account.
Folder backup unavailableUse Chrome or Edge on a computer, or Download backup instead.
The currency is wrongSettings & backup → Currency, or type your own symbol. Amounts are not converted.
I want the tour againSettings & backup → Welcome tour → Show tour.
